title: Modelling Infectious Disease in Southeast Asia - Forum for Inclusive Exchange of Sustained Transformative Actions (MIDSEA-FIESTA)
text:
Day: Monday 4 May, morning · Lead: Wirichada Pan-ngum
The opening session moved from introductions through to the formation of working subgroups for the week. Participants began by sharing their research interests, network experiences, wish lists for MIDSEA, and the skills and time they could contribute. This was followed by an orientation to the week’s working principles: flexibility, concrete deliverables across short and long time horizons, sustainable participation styles, and meaningful engagement of early-career (ECR) and mid-career researchers (MCR).
A group discussion and SWOT analysis then explored why networks matter, what makes regional networks in Asia distinct, and how theory-of-change thinking could guide MIDSEA’s growth. The session then turned to co-creating MIDSEA’s long-term vision and core values, drawing on the SEADREAM draft proposal, with discussion of branding, network alliances, and participants’ aspirations for MIDSEA in 5 and 10 years.
The session concluded with the formation of six working subgroups:

Day: Monday 4 May, afternoon · Coordination: Bimandra Adiputra Djaafara
Subgroups held initial discussions and began drafting their plans. End-of-day verbal reports were collected. The research collaboration subgroup polled members on thematic research interests to inform Wednesday’s research themes workshop. The welcome dinner provided informal networking time.



Day: Tuesday 5 May, morning · Speaker: Jomar F. Rabajante
A technical lecture on the mathematical derivation of the basic reproduction number R0 in heterogeneous population models, covering the next-generation matrix approach and its implications for disease control thresholds in structured populations.



Day: Tuesday 5 May, morning · Coordination: Bimandra Adiputra Djaafara
Each subgroup produced a structured written plan covering objectives, planned activities, milestones, evaluation criteria, and resource needs. Plans were shared across subgroups for peer comment in the afternoon.



Day: Tuesday 5 May, afternoon
Subgroups reviewed and commented on one another’s draft plans asynchronously via shared documents. Subgroups then revise plans in light of feedback and identify minimum resource requirements for each activity. A collective brainstorm generated ideas for resourcing strategies, including grant applications, host-institution underwriting, and voluntary effort.



Day: Wednesday 6 May, morning · Speaker: Nguyen Duy Tung
A technical lecture on environmental datasets available in Southeast Asia - including land use, climate, and ecological data - and their role in parameterising and validating infectious disease models. The session introduced data sources and methodological approaches for integrating environmental drivers into models.



Day: Wednesday 6 May, morning · Lead: Keisuke Ejima
Participants identified and mapped priority research themes for MIDSEA collaborative work. Breakout discussions covered the current status of work in each area, key open questions, and which MIDSEA members were active in each theme. A shortlist was agreed for further development on Thursday.



Day: Wednesday 6 May, afternoon · Coordinator: Phrutsamon Wongnak
Half-day excursion to Hong Island, providing informal networking time between participants.



Day: Thursday 7 May, morning · Speaker: Kiesha Prem
A technical lecture on approaches to measuring and modelling social contact patterns, covering novel data collection methods, their use in age-structured transmission models, and implications for intervention design.



Day: Thursday 7 May, morning · Lead: Norvin P. Bansilan
The session mapped existing mechanisms to enable research across MIDSEA: grant funding sources, student recruitment pathways, mobility schemes for students and faculty, and institutional agreements. Participants identified key barriers - fragmented funding landscapes, visa constraints, limited mobility schemes - and opportunities across the regional ecosystem.



Day: Thursday 7 May, afternoon
Research theme groups produced structured written roadmaps covering objectives, activities, milestones, evaluation indicators, responsibilities, meeting cadence, communication methods, and resources needed. Preliminary concept notes for grants, collaborative research, or papers were drafted where time permitted.



Day: Friday 8 May, morning · Lecturers: Wirichada Pan-ngum and Hannah Clapham
Introduction to key grant writing principles - conceptual framework, theory of change, measurable milestones, and alignment with funder priorities - followed by direct feedback on each research theme’s concept note, identifying strengths, gaps, and positioning opportunities. Research theme groups presented concept notes to the full group receiving comments in light of the grant writing discussions. The session closed with a synthesis of all FIESTA outputs - subgroup plans, research roadmaps, and enabling strategies - and confirmed next steps and responsibilities for the MIDSEA network going forward.



Day: Friday 8 May, afternoon · Lead: Thitiya Theparod
Country teams present status quo, case studies, and prospective plans for cross-learning. The countries included the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Laos PDR, and Thailand.

title: MIDSEA Summer School 2026 at UNIMAS in Kuching, Malaysia
text:
MIDSEA Summer School 2026 at UNIMAS in Kuching, Malaysia: Strengthened Networks for Shared Knowledge and Future Public Health

Building regional public health capacity
Following successful editions in the scenic coastal city of Quy Nhon, Vietnam, in 2024, and in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, home to the world-famous 9th-century UNESCO World Heritage temple complexes of Borobudur and Prambanan in 2025, the third MIDSEA Summer School continued in Sarawak, Malaysia. Held from 8 to 12 June 2026 at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS) in Kuching, brought together MIDSEAers from local researchers, academics, public health practitioner, and emerging talents from Southeast Asia, India, Korea, Japan, and Australia to exchange knowledge and strengthen collaboration in infectious disease modelling. Set on the rainforest island of Borneo, the world’s third-largest island and a place rich in wildlife and ancient ecologies, the summer school further reinforced MIDSEA’s commitment to regional capacity building, and public health in climate resilience.


Training in Real-World Public Health Challenges
Hosted by the CSIT faculty at UNIMAS, the MIDSEA Summer School served as a space for technical training, cross-disciplinary research discussions, international networking, and cultural exchange. Created a learning environment where scientific knowledge could connect with regional collaboration and practical public health action.
During the 5 days, MIDSEAers learned from experts from leading regional and international institutions; the National University of Singapore, Mahidol University, Mahasarakham University, Nanyang Technological University, the University of the Philippines Mindanao, the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit, Melbourne University, Monash University, and UNIMAS. Organized in collaboration with the Australian Government’s SPARKLE Programme and the Wellcome-funded Dengue Modelling Consortium, focused on equipping the next generation of infectious disease modelers and public health practitioners with tools to support outbreak preparedness and response.
MIDSEAers joined their preferred four intensive training tracks. Track 1, Modelling 101, introduced early-career and newMIDSEAers to core concepts. Track 2, Simulation, and Track 3, Inference, helped the modelers strengthen their skills and apply more advanced techniques. Track 4, Modelling Heterogeneities, focused on integrating the complexity of infectious disease dynamics into more realistic public health challenges and solutions. Together, these tracks guided MIDSEAers from foundational concepts to advanced disease modelling techniques, epidemiological analysis, programming, simulation, computational methods, and operations research.


Preparing for Tomorrow’s Challenges
From knowledge to practice, MIDSEAers engaged in real-world public health concerns through intensive regional case studies and practice projects on dengue, rabies, influenza, COVID-19, HIV and RSV. Helping the modeler understand how modelling can support outbreak preparedness and decision-making. The training and workshop brought together parallel learning tracks, specialized plenary workshops, operations research sessions, MIDSEAers’s own research poster presentations, and collaborative group work. Together, these activities helped bridge the gap between infectious disease projections and practical public health decisions, while also showcasing emerging research from MIDSEAers and experts across the region and beyond.

“…This opportunity was a doorway to a lifetime of “firsts”: my first airplane ride, my first time traveling internationally, and my very first poster presentation. …. Placed in Track 2: Simulations, I realized how vast the ocean of epidemiology truly is, taking a “first swim” in the vast sea of global academia is daunting, but this community made the water feel incredibly welcoming….” Jericho Roland Sueno MIDSEAer 2026, Ateneo de Manila University, the Philippines



A Glimpse of Borneo’s Wild Side: A reflection of Climate and Health
After days of intense and deep modelling sessions, workshops, and discussions, MIDSEAers stepped outside the classroom to meet another side of Borneo. A visit to the Semenggoh Wildlife Centre offered a close look at orangutans in their protected habitat and a chance to reflect on how deeply human health is linked with the natural world. MIDSEAers were exposed to a reminder that climate change, shifting environments, wildlife habitats, and infectious disease risks are all part of the same bigger story. The day ended with good food and good conversation, as MIDSEAers continued exchanging ideas and building friendships across the region with delicious local Sarawakian cuisine and dishes.


Strengthening Capacity, Sustaining Collaboration
With the Philippines set to host the next MIDSEA Summer School in 2027 on its second largest islands with rich and diverse of sanctuaries, cultures and warming people, the network looks ready for even deeper collaboration and a shared commitment to public health security in our ‘middle of the SEA’.
–Vidhyakorn Mahd-Adam

title: MIDSEA Summer School x IWOMB: HULMA Summit 2027
text:
After 3 amazing editions of our beloved MIDSEA Summer School, 2027 brings something special: we’re joining forces with the International Workshop on Mathematical Biology (IWOMB) to bring our two communities together for a special edition → the 2027 HULMA Summit!
And we’re not stopping there. Beyond the packed learning during school/workshop days, we’re upgrading our vibrant research poster sessions into a 2-day symposium with abstract submission! Get ready for an exciting week of science, collaboration, and Southeast Asian chaotic fun .
Whether you’re a student, researcher, or professional in mathematical biology or data science, filling out our Expression of Interest Survey will help us tailor this premier 3-in-1 event—summer school, workshop, and symposium—around you.

🗓 Date: June 6–11, 2027
📍 Venue: Discovery Samal, Davao del Norte, Philippines
💡 Theme: Modeling Across Scales, from Biological Dynamics to Public Health Decisions

title: MIDSEA Summer School 2026
text:
MIDSEA Summer School 2026 at UNIMAS in Kuching, Malaysia: Strengthened Networks for Shared Knowledge and Future Public Health

Building regional public health capacity
Following successful editions in the scenic coastal city of Quy Nhon, Vietnam, in 2024, and in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, home to the world-famous 9th-century UNESCO World Heritage temple complexes of Borobudur and Prambanan in 2025, the third MIDSEA Summer School continued in Sarawak, Malaysia. Held from 8 to 12 June 2026 at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS) in Kuching, brought together MIDSEAers from local researchers, academics, public health practitioner, and emerging talents from Southeast Asia, India, Korea, Japan, and Australia to exchange knowledge and strengthen collaboration in infectious disease modelling. Set on the rainforest island of Borneo, the world’s third-largest island and a place rich in wildlife and ancient ecologies, the summer school further reinforced MIDSEA’s commitment to regional capacity building, and public health in climate resilience.


Training in Real-World Public Health Challenges
Hosted by the CSIT faculty at UNIMAS, the MIDSEA Summer School served as a space for technical training, cross-disciplinary research discussions, international networking, and cultural exchange. Created a learning environment where scientific knowledge could connect with regional collaboration and practical public health action.
During the 5 days, MIDSEAers learned from experts from leading regional and international institutions; the National University of Singapore, Mahidol University, Mahasarakham University, Nanyang Technological University, the University of the Philippines Mindanao, the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit, Melbourne University, Monash University, and UNIMAS. Organized in collaboration with the Australian Government’s SPARKLE Programme and the Wellcome-funded Dengue Modelling Consortium, focused on equipping the next generation of infectious disease modelers and public health practitioners with tools to support outbreak preparedness and response.
MIDSEAers joined their preferred four intensive training tracks. Track 1, Modelling 101, introduced early-career and newMIDSEAers to core concepts. Track 2, Simulation, and Track 3, Inference, helped the modelers strengthen their skills and apply more advanced techniques. Track 4, Modelling Heterogeneities, focused on integrating the complexity of infectious disease dynamics into more realistic public health challenges and solutions. Together, these tracks guided MIDSEAers from foundational concepts to advanced disease modelling techniques, epidemiological analysis, programming, simulation, computational methods, and operations research.


Preparing for Tomorrow’s Challenges
From knowledge to practice, MIDSEAers engaged in real-world public health concerns through intensive regional case studies and practice projects on dengue, rabies, influenza, COVID-19, HIV and RSV. Helping the modeler understand how modelling can support outbreak preparedness and decision-making. The training and workshop brought together parallel learning tracks, specialized plenary workshops, operations research sessions, MIDSEAers’s own research poster presentations, and collaborative group work. Together, these activities helped bridge the gap between infectious disease projections and practical public health decisions, while also showcasing emerging research from MIDSEAers and experts across the region and beyond.

“…This opportunity was a doorway to a lifetime of “firsts”: my first airplane ride, my first time traveling internationally, and my very first poster presentation. …. Placed in Track 2: Simulations, I realized how vast the ocean of epidemiology truly is, taking a “first swim” in the vast sea of global academia is daunting, but this community made the water feel incredibly welcoming….” Jericho Roland Sueno MIDSEAer 2026, Ateneo de Manila University, the Philippines



A Glimpse of Borneo’s Wild Side: A reflection of Climate and Health
After days of intense and deep modelling sessions, workshops, and discussions, MIDSEAers stepped outside the classroom to meet another side of Borneo. A visit to the Semenggoh Wildlife Centre offered a close look at orangutans in their protected habitat and a chance to reflect on how deeply human health is linked with the natural world. MIDSEAers were exposed to a reminder that climate change, shifting environments, wildlife habitats, and infectious disease risks are all part of the same bigger story. The day ended with good food and good conversation, as MIDSEAers continued exchanging ideas and building friendships across the region with delicious local Sarawakian cuisine and dishes.


Strengthening Capacity, Sustaining Collaboration
With the Philippines set to host the next MIDSEA Summer School in 2027 on its second largest islands with rich and diverse of sanctuaries, cultures and warming people, the network looks ready for even deeper collaboration and a shared commitment to public health security in our ‘middle of the SEA’.
–Vidhyakorn Mahd-Adam
